hero.title: A better workflow for collaborating *with AI agents*.
hero.subtitle: Intent and decisions stay with you; agents do the work in between, with a clear handoff at every step. I build this workflow in the open as four pieces you can use together or alone: isolated task spaces, intent in your own words, staged runs with a human gate at each stage, and a window that shows what every agent is doing.

hero.name: workbranch
hero.tagline: One task folder per feature. *Every repo in one place.*
hero.subtitle: Manage Git worktree task spaces without memorizing git worktree commands. Create a task folder across one repo or many, keep base branches fresh with short, safe commands, and see which AI agent is waiting on you from the menu bar.
hero.platforms: macOS · Linux · MIT · Companion for macOS
hero.figure_alt: workbranch creates one task folder across multiple repositories, and Companion shows each task's AI agent sessions in waiting-on-you, running, and turn-ended columns.

features.title: Create with the CLI. Watch with Companion.
features.subtitle: The CLI runs the Git and worktree flow. Companion reads what the agents report and shows it in the menu bar. Nothing else changes about how you work.

items.title: One task folder, every repo
items.description: workbranch add login creates feat-login/ with a linked worktree for each configured repo, while _base/ keeps the shared base checkouts. The task root is where your AI agent runs; the repos live underneath it.
points: Works with one repo or many, so an agent can touch frontend and backend in one session
workbranch init registers the project and can create the first task on the spot
Stacked on a feature base? add asks only for the task name and derives feature-cpq-login/

items.title: Refresh every repo in one command
items.description: pull brings the bases from their remotes, update applies them to a task, and refresh does both. Before an agent starts, one command puts every repo in the task on the latest base.
points: update and refresh stop on a dirty worktree instead of merging over your changes
workbranch stash keeps changes under the current branch, not the stash list every worktree shares
finalize runs pull → update → land in one go

items.title: Two ways to ship
items.description: What push publishes depends on your base. On main, push the task branch and open a PR. On a feature branch, land the stacked task into it and push the base.
points: Feature flow: workbranch push feat-login
Stacked flow: workbranch land feat-login-part1, then workbranch push
prune removes clean task workspaces already merged into local bases

items.title: See which agent is waiting on you
items.description: Workbranch Companion is a macOS menu bar app. It reads hook observations from Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Build and places each task on a board: waiting on you, running, or turn ended and ready for review.
points: Task cards show IDE, Terminal, and Finder launchers plus each repo's branch and Git facts without expanding
Click a card for recent commits and session details; double-click opens the task in your IDE
Base repositories show branch, dirty state, and ahead/behind counts with PULL, PUSH, or CHECK guidance

items.title: Token usage, read locally
items.description: A usage summary above the board shows Claude Code and Codex side by side: plan limits with time to reset, today's tokens, and the last seven days. Companion reads only local files and never signs in.
points: Pick what shows beside the menu bar icon, as used or remaining percent
Usage view adds a shared 14-day daily chart and a last-7-days table
Opt in to Live Claude Limits to refresh while a Claude Code session is open

items.title: Works with the agents you already run
items.description: Install hooks for Claude Code or Codex with one command and review the provider's hook trust. Grok Build needs explicit trust: inspect the plugin source first, then install with --trust.
points: No TASK-WORKBRANCH.md reporting required; runtime snapshots come from hooks
Companion onboarding can install the CLI with Homebrew and connect agents for you
One update action upgrades the CLI before Companion

hero.name: Tasteful Intent
hero.tagline: Write the intent in your own words. *Keep it as local Markdown.*
hero.subtitle: Prompts change from one request to the next. Your intent and taste last longer. Tasteful Intent keeps that source in a Human workspace and opens what AI makes in a separate AI workspace, without replacing the original.
hero.platforms: macOS · Apple silicon & Intel · Tauri 2 · signed and notarized
hero.figure_alt: Tasteful Intent, a local Markdown app with separate Human and AI workspaces.

features.title: Intent first. Results kept apart.
features.subtitle: The app does not run an LLM or copy your notes into its own database. It works directly with the folders you select.

items.title: Human workspace: your originals
items.description: Write Human notes with CodeMirror 6 and GFM rendering. Autosave every 500 ms, atomic writes, and external-change protection keep the file safe. The filename is the document title.
points: New documents start with created and updated timestamps and an empty body
Create, rename, move, and send files or folders to the Trash from keyboard-accessible context menus
Sort by latest update or title; switch the list between Full, Medium, and Simple density

items.title: AI workspace: results, kept apart
items.description: Open multiple AI folders as tabs. Pin frequent roots with a one- or two-character label and restore each folder's document session when you come back.
points: AI folders allow Markdown editing and new documents, but no other structural file operations
Closing a tab changes only app settings; it never deletes the folder or its files
Scanning respects .gitignore and .ignore and skips hidden paths and symlinks

items.title: Edit → View → Split
items.description: Keep several documents open and move each one through Edit, View, and Split. Human documents start in Edit; AI documents start in View.
points: ⌘F or Ctrl+F finds text in the current document with highlighted matches in every mode
Root-relative local images render up to 10 MiB
Export the current rendered document as a PDF

items.title: Local by design
items.description: Every selected root is canonicalized and file operations stay inside that boundary. Human deletion uses the macOS Trash instead of permanent removal. Settings live in the OS app-data directory.
points: No built-in LLM runtime, no accounts, no sync
Nothing is copied into an app database; the Markdown files are the source
Workspace-wide search, tags, and backlinks are outside the current scope

items.title: Small, finished details
items.description: Three panes, two panes, or content-only mode. English and Korean UI, four themes, four Human/AI color palettes, and two writing typefaces.
points: ⌘1 toggles the folder pane, ⌘2 toggles content-only mode
Signed and notarized DMGs for Apple silicon and Intel on every release
Built with Tauri 2 and Rust, React 19, TypeScript, and CodeMirror 6

hero.name: skills
hero.tagline: From intent to signoff, *one stage at a time.*
hero.subtitle: Agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, and other skill-aware agents. The main piece is tk workflow: a staged, document-driven way to take one change from intent to signoff. It runs with one agent, and other agents join for review and debate when you ask.
hero.platforms: Claude Code · Codex · Grok · any skill-aware agent
hero.figure_alt: tk workflow: five stages (intent, plan, implement, verify, signoff) run left to right with a human approval gate between each, in three parts: you lead and AI sharpens (intent, plan), hand off (implement), check together (verify, signoff). tk-check runs the repo's typecheck, lint, format, tests and build for implement and verify. Intents are permanent, tasks are per piece of work, specs describe current behaviour.

features.title: Five stages. Files are the state.
features.subtitle: Each stage reads a document and writes a document. Where work stands is derived from docs/, never from conversation memory, so any session can pick it up.

items.title: Files are the state
items.description: Intents are permanent, one per change. plan.md and todo.md live only for the current piece of work and are emptied at signoff. Specs describe how each module behaves now, in timeless language.
points: docs/intents/<MODULE><NNN>-<slug>.md holds why, what, non-goals, R-numbered requirements, and the outcome
docs/tasks/ holds the plan, the todo list, and each peer's reviews and debates
tk-setup explores the repo once and writes docs/agents/tk-workflow.md

items.title: A human gate at every stage
items.description: A stage saves its artifact, prints a summary, and ends the turn. The next stage starts only on an explicit next. Hedged answers are not approval; the driver asks again.
points: tk-intent interviews you against the code and numbers requirements R1, R2, …
tk-plan turns the intent into vertical slices, each Backend → Frontend, with an R-id coverage matrix
tk-implement checks boxes with evidence and runs a tk-check checkpoint after every sub-phase, fixing what fails

items.title: Multi-agent review and debate
items.description: Say review or debate and other agents (claude, codex, grok) read the artifact or argue one open decision. They run headless, read-only, one process each. Their answers land in files, and one agent still does all the editing.
points: tk-multi-review triages findings into patches, tk-grill questions, or deferred notes
tk-multi-debate runs two written rounds, then the human decides through tk-grill
Inside herdr the peers run in a sibling pane so you can watch; outside, they run directly

items.title: The agent never commits
items.description: It reads git, it does not write it. Commits, pushes, and branches are yours. tk-check runs typecheck, lint with warnings failing, format check, and tests at every checkpoint, and fixes what fails without silencing the tools. Before signoff, tk-verify runs them again with the plan's behaviour checks and audits the work.
points: tk-signoff traces every R-id through plan, diff, and verification, then decides Go or No-Go
On Go it appends the intent Outcome, updates module specs, and empties docs/tasks/
Git history is the archive

hero.name: tkhwang-herdr-mods
hero.tagline: One window for every agent. *Kept as files.*
hero.subtitle: The Herdr app is where the agents run. These mods make its window show what matters: branch and PR status per space, agents grouped under their space with status glows, yellow agent tabs, a commit graph, and a Changes panel with an AI commit message and a Push button. The layout and every patched mod live in one repo; one script applies them and backs them up.
hero.platforms: Herdr app · macOS · Apache-2.0 · third-party mods under their own licenses
hero.figure_alt: A schematic of the Herdr window that layouts/main-dev.json builds: better-spaces and agents-dev in the sidebar, tabs-dev as the tab bar, git-graph, better-changes and files-dev stacked in the side panel, and a terminal running ./sync.sh apply in the center.

features.title: One layout. Patched mods. One sync script.
features.subtitle: Herdr keeps its layout and mods in ~/.config/herdr-app. This repo holds copies of the ones I changed, each patch marked with a comment, and sync.sh moves them in and out.

items.title: The window, as files
items.description: layouts/main-dev.json is a clone of Herdr's main layout whose blocks point at the mods here. ./sync.sh apply copies the layout, settings, keys, and mods into ~/.config/herdr-app; ./sync.sh backup copies them back after you change something in the app.
points: Every file apply replaces is moved to ~/.config/herdr-app.bak-<time>-<pid>/ first
Copies are staged beside the app folder and checked with herdr-app check before any goes in; one rejected mod installs nothing
Only the mods and files named in sync.sh are touched; other mods in the app folder stay as they are

items.title: Spaces and agents, with status you can see
items.description: better-spaces shows branch and PR status per space, nested worktrees, and dev server ports. agents-dev groups agents under their space. Both glow green when an agent is done and orange when it is blocked, and breathe while it works; the current space is tinted cyan.
points: better-spaces is munza/herdr-mods with the status glows of filipores/herdr-spaces-status merged in
agents-dev steps each agent row in under its space header, so the space reads as the heading
A space in a workbranch wrapper folder, not a repo itself, shows no branch or PR

items.title: A tab bar that points at the agents
items.description: tabs-dev tints any tab with an agent yellow and keeps every tab at least 180px wide. Git and Markdown buttons open git-graph in the side panel and a Markdown preview in the center, a 3 | 2 column switch zooms the agent pane, and the + menu gets Open with Zed.
points: 2 columns folds the shell column away and keeps the file panel; 3 columns unzooms only what it zoomed
The Markdown button renders the file Files previews or Changes picked, one viewer tab per space
herdr-open-with-zed opens the focused terminal's folder in zed, else zeditor, else open -a Zed

items.title: Changes, with an AI message and a Push button
items.description: better-changes groups staged and unstaged files, shows inline or side-by-side diffs, and in a folder of repos adds a repo picker. A sparkle Message button writes the commit message from the staged diff and the last 8 messages; Push sends HEAD to its upstream and shows how far ahead it is.
points: Message runs claude -p with no tools and the sonnet model, so the staged diff goes to Anthropic through your Claude Code login; change AI_COMMAND for codex or grok
Push never forces; a rejected push shows git's reason as a note, and the button is off on a detached HEAD or without a remote
The buttons keep their look while the panel rereads git, and a press during that runs as soon as it ends

items.title: A commit graph and a Markdown preview
items.description: git-graph draws the focused repo's history after VS Code's Git Graph: colored lanes, branch and tag labels, an uncommitted row, details and diffs, and a right-click menu that asks before it acts. In a folder of repos it shows a Manygit list instead. markdown-browser renders the picked Markdown file in a center tab.
points: Six review fixes are patched in: non-ASCII file names, untracked diffs, a refresh after git add, prompts off for fetch and pull, dialogs that stay open, no double start
git reaches the network only on Fetch, Pull, Push, or deleting a remote branch; the mod asks GitHub's releases API once a day, which Stop checking turns off
Herdr stops a command after 30 s, so a slow fetch or push can fail there

items.title: Patches you can find, licenses you can read
items.description: Every change to an upstream mod is marked with a comment, so grep -rn "status glow" mods finds all of it. Clones of Herdr's own mods get no updates: after Herdr changes one, clone it again and re-apply the marked patch. Each third-party mod keeps its license file; the two without one are downloaded by apply at pinned commits.
points: 18 markers, among them dev ports, status glow, current highlight, tab kind, view mode, ai message, push button, and review fixes
markdown.js is one file kept in tabs-dev, files-dev, and better-changes: change all three together
copy-on-select and the Catppuccin themes are fetched at pinned commits, the themes checked by sha256
